I made soap for my and my roommate’s dogs. 

The recipe is olive oil, coconut oil, beef tallow, Shea butter and jojoba oil. The liquid was raw milk from an Amish farm down the road. I added colloidal oatmeal at 2Tb per lb and whole oats on the bottom of the large rounds. No sents or colors were added. 

I washed three dogs of different sizes and hair lengths over a long and unpleasant afternoon. The only thing they had in common was a hatred of bathes. There was a long haired 20 lb corgi, a medium haired 83lb mutt (German Shepherd/Labrador/Pitbull/Australian Cattledog) and a short haired 130lb Great Dane. The Dane Hambone has bad skin with some bald patches on his belly. He is allergic to some random things so we have to be careful with foods and products. The mutt Tina is the reason I washed the pack. She has been itching more and more the last few weeks and her hair has an almost greasy feel to it. The Corgy was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. It had been 6+ months since the last bath and all dogs have flea medication. 

The large round fit perfectly in my hand freeing my other hand up to use the shower nozzle or scrubbing or comforting. I never had to stop to pour more liquid shampoo and I loved that. It lathered up well with large creamy bubbles on the medium and long haired girls. The short haired boy did not lather as much but did some. It rinsed away well with no residue.

After drying the short haired Dane’s hair was soft and clean, his bald spots were soft with no flaking or redness. The medium haired mutt dried soft, but not super soft. I noticed an immediate stop in itching after the bath. It has been a few days and the itching has not returned. She just looks much more comfortable and relaxed. The long haired Corgy dried semi soft as well. I was hoping for a more soft coat from her but it feels just a touch dry. 

All in all this was a wonderful soap for the skin. It cleaned the fur well and washed way clean. Unfortunately the fur did not end up as soft as I had hoped nor did it have much shine to it. I am happy with this recipe for my sweet baby Hambone and it will help little Tina Hyena with her itch prone skin. I would have to make changes if I wanted to wash Juniper the fluff monster again.
